question.question: When an unaligned batched-log append needs a previously persisted prefix after a cache miss, can a KV read error be treated as absence and cause a successful write to discard that prefix?
question.importance: Silent loss of previously stored log entries can invalidate recovery and replication history. The immediate subject is persistence semantics; no cluster-level data-loss endpoint has been executed.
contexts: Unaligned append in an existing batch
Explicit read error, with stored bytes still present
event_paths: engine SaveRaftState -> db.saveRaftState -> recordBatch -> getMergedFirstBatch -> cache miss/GetValue -> CommitWriteBatch -> read persisted batch

supporting_behavior_ids.B-persistence: Engine treats a returned SaveRaftState error as fatal, so swallowed error bypasses caller handling.
supporting_behavior_ids.B-formation: Stored entry history constrains commitment/replication in the A1 relationship supported by this storage question.

counterevidence: A cache hit avoids GetValue, so a simple hot-cache append would not exercise this premise.
Aligned batch replacement requires no old prefix.
The engine panics on a returned persistence error; a check must distinguish proper rejection from successful destructive replacement.
unknowns: Establish actual cache-miss caller history and inject only a GetValue error, without deleting stored data or replacing target merge logic.
Measure append result and persisted prefix separately; a read error alone is not evidence of data loss.
question.trigger_rationale: Pebble GetValue explicitly returns non-not-found errors, but batch lookup discards their cause and merge treats false as no old data. A clean reopen plus one read failure discriminates this from the protective cache path; source lookup is more valuable than ambiguous result-buffer mutation.

rationale: Select the sourced cold-cache error-handling discrepancy in persisted history rather than presume a contract for arbitrary result-buffer mutation.

feedback.answered: The transport interface explicitly allows out-of-order message delivery, supporting the accepted read-context schedule. The NodeUser.ReadIndex path lacks immediate setStepReady, but the in-repository tick worker independently schedules every cluster; this excludes an unsupported claim of permanently lost continuation from the missing local signal alone. Snapshot status has a dedicated delayed queue, advanced by node ticks and drained by normal message handling, followed by retry/heartbeat continuation. Result.Data ownership remains ambiguous after tracing exports; no mutation experiment was manufactured.
remaining: Investigate actual persisted-prefix effects of a reported KV read error on a cold unaligned batch append.
Result.Data ownership and timing-qualified membership/read authority remain independent unresolved source questions.
feedback.rationale: Retain composed protections and the explicit ordering contract; focus execution effort on a concrete error/absence conflation.
